beats.narration_text: This week we kick off a new research track in Security and Exploitation for Physical A I. In static image classification, a tiny perturbation only has to fool a single frame. But in a closed-loop robot running at twenty hertz, can a visual patch smoothly steer a clean Vision-Language-Action model toward a decoy object without touching the user's prompt?

props.command: Can a test-time visual patch smoothly steer a clean OpenVLA-7B robot toward a decoy object without altering the prompt, and how do we defend against it?
output: 23 papers surveyed across VLA attacks & shields

beats.narration_text: Here is the core gap we found across twenty-three recent papers. Existing visual patches on standard V L A models only make the robot arm freeze, twitch, or miss. Smoothly hijacking a clean model's multi-step trajectory requires tricking its semantic object representationâ€”not forcing raw motor actions.

beats.narration_text: Following peer feedback from Dev, we eliminated fragile coordinate matching and designed a two-stage simulation pipeline on LIBERO and Open V L A seven B. During training, differentiable Kornia homography warps a tabletop coaster patch across camera angles; at test time, native MuJoCo rendering evaluates closed-loop control alongside our spatial consistency shield.

props.title: Blind Patch Training to Closed-Loop Shield.

phases.label: Blind patch update
phases.desc: Attention Magnet or Vision Feature Copy

beats.narration_text: Why does our second attack methodâ€”the Auto-Feature Copy Patchâ€”matter so much for iteration speed? Because Open V L A computes its two hundred fifty-six visual tokens inside a zero point six billion parameter vision encoder before the seven billion parameter Llama two backbone. By targeting the vision encoder directly, we cut training memory from sixteen gigabytes down to four.

We paired these two attack mechanisms with a stronger runtime defense. Dev noted that five random masks often miss a small patch or let the poisoned view win a median vote. So we upgraded our shield to a systematic three-by-three covering grid with two-round minority verification and a three-step persistence rule to keep false positives below five percent per episode.

terms.definition: Pulls 100% of Llama-2 text-to-image cross-attention onto the patch squares.
Copies top-3 clean object tokens in SigLIP + DINOv2 using 3-4 GB VRAM.
Guarantees one mask covers the patch; 2-round check cuts false alarms < 5%.

beats.narration_text: That gives us a concrete six-week, two-engineer execution plan. Weeks one through three build the shared LIBERO harness, PyTorch attention hooks, and Kornia patch trainer. Weeks four through six split into parallel tracks to benchmark Attention Magnet, Auto-Feature Copy, and the combined patch on Targeted Steering Success Rate and kinematic jerk.
